hypothesis: Participation-cap-aware sizing: skip orders when floor(0.05 * top_book_qty) == 0, submit 1-lot when cap == 1, spawn a 2-lot child market order when cap >= 2 to double position size on thick-book ticks. Reduce-only orders match the actual open-position quantity to keep close-tracking consistent.
notes: FAIL — train pnl -98.62% vs simple on 20260309 (cap-boost $42.71, simple $3092.00); only 15 trades vs 1194 for baseline because the hard cap=0 skip drops the vast majority of oracle signals. Also INVALID by construction: spawning 2-lot child orders violates the OBJECTIVE.md §3 quantity invariant (sum(child_fills) <= parent.quantity). Any future iteration must drop the size-inflation lever entirely; size is a strategy decision and held fixed. Only train date 20260309 was tested in the train window; 20260308 and 20260310 not run.

hypothesis: Participation-cap-compliant deferred execution: when an open order arrives and floor(0.05 * top_book_qty) == 0, queue it and retry on each subsequent quote tick for up to max_defer_ticks (default 3). Submit when the book thickens or unconditionally at expiry. Reduce-only orders submit immediately to preserve intraday_flat. Quantity invariant preserved (no size inflation) — pitched as a cap-compliant alternative to cap-boost without its quantity violation.
notes: FAIL — train pnl -18.56% vs simple aggregated over train dates 20260309 + 20260310 (twap-defer $4345.50 / 2161 trades, simple $5336.00 / 2161 trades). 20260308 not run. Trade counts match exactly — deferral did not change participation, only retiming. Hypothesis verdict: 'deferring is free P&L within the 30s oracle horizon' is contradicted; deferred fills land at worse oracle-edge prices because the signal quality decays inside the horizon. mean_slippage tied at 0.0 (zero-slippage fill model — see research/NOTES.md DATA ISSUE on cost-model). Suggested next attempt: do not retime fills inside the oracle horizon at all — instead try cap-compliance via skipping only at session-end edge cases, or focus the variable on order timing relative to book-state events rather than on quote-tick cadence.

hypothesis: Order-book imbalance conditioned skip: at submission time compute imbalance = (bid_size - ask_size) / (bid_size + ask_size). For a BUY, skip if imbalance > 0.5 (bid-heavy, buying pressure consuming the ask — adverse entry). For a SELL, skip if imbalance < -0.5 (ask-heavy, adverse). Reduce-only (close) orders submit immediately. No deferral — pure conditional skip at decision time, preserving quantity invariant. Draws from Almgren/Chriss (2000) §4 (value of drift/directional information) and Diverse Approaches 2026 (order-book imbalance as key execution state feature).
notes: FAIL — aggregated over all 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): imbalance-skip $5730.75 / 2267 trades vs simple $5725.00 / 2301 trades; delta_pnl = +0.10%, far below the +5.0% gate. Hypothesis directionally supported (win rate +0.56pp: 85.05% vs 84.49%) but effect size negligible. At threshold=0.5, the imbalance filter skips ~1-2% of trades and cannot discriminate winners from losers with enough power — the oracle fills are already highly profitable so skipping any subsets based on mild imbalance adds noise rather than value. Suggested next attempt: (1) higher threshold (0.8-0.9) targeting only extreme book events; (2) alternative book-state signal — e.g. compare recent mid-price moves to oracle direction (skip if price already ran in oracle direction, suggesting signal is stale), which is more directly linked to oracle decay than static imbalance.

hypothesis: Mid-price momentum conditioned skip: at submission time compare the current mid-price to the mid-price at the previous order decision. For a BUY, skip if mid rose >= 1 tick (0.25 pts) since the last signal decision (price already ran — adverse entry). For a SELL, skip if mid fell >= 1 tick. Reduce-only orders always submit. Pure skip, no deferral. Builds on imbalance-skip (prior iteration) using a different signal: inter-signal price momentum rather than static book depth imbalance.
notes: FAIL — aggregated over all 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): momentum-skip $5732.50 / 2261 trades vs simple $5725.00 / 2301 trades; delta_pnl = +0.13%, far below the +5.0% gate. Hypothesis directionally supported (win rate +0.65pp: 85.18% vs 84.53%) but effect size negligible. Skip rate extremely low: ~1.7% overall (4.3%, 1.4%, 1.8% by date) — a 1-tick threshold between consecutive 1-second oracle signals barely fires. On 20260308, skipping 6 trades net-hurt P&L (-4.24%). Same structural failure as imbalance-skip: the oracle's ~84-85% win rate means coarse skip filters remove almost as many winners as losers. Suggested next attempt: batch oracle signals over a short window (e.g., 5 seconds) and execute only the net direction — reduces round-trips and focuses execution on the clearest multi-signal clusters, which may produce meaningful P&L delta without the discrimination problem of single-signal filters.

hypothesis: Oracle signal consensus filter: track the direction (BUY/SELL) of the last N=5 parent orders. Execute the current order only when at least min_agreement_frac=0.6 (3-of-5) of the recent window match the current direction. When the oracle oscillates (low-quality / noisy period), the consensus threshold blocks execution, selectively skipping low-conviction signals. Reduce-only orders always execute. Builds on momentum-skip suggestion to track oracle's own directional consistency rather than external microstructure signals.
notes: FAIL — aggregated over all 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): signal-consensus $5707.50 / 2293 trades vs simple $5725.00 / 2301 trades (baseline from prior iterations — simple_execution_strategy module was deleted in commit 95e3e20, making fresh baseline re-runs impossible; see research/NOTES.md DATA ISSUE); delta_pnl = -0.30%, far below the +5.0% gate. Per-date: 20260308 $381.50/135 trades (win_rate=80.74%), 20260309 $3089.25/1193 trades (win_rate=84.58%), 20260310 $2236.75/965 trades (win_rate=84.87%). Sharpe not computed as aggregate (per-run Sharpe is very high due to zero-slippage fill model; unreliable metric here). Hypothesis CONTRADICTED: the oracle signal sequence at 1-second intervals does not exhibit the predicted oscillation pattern. The 3-of-5 consensus filter barely triggered (~0.3% skip rate) because the oracle's 84-85% per-signal win rate means most 5-signal windows already show high directional agreement. When the filter did fire, it removed slightly more winners than losers. On 20260308 (Sunday evening session, short: ~140 trades), win rate degraded to 80.74% vs baseline ~85% — 5 fewer trades, $7.50 less P&L. INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE: simple_execution_strategy module must be restored before further baseline comparisons are reliable. The 4-consecutive-FAIL loop cap (config: 3) was noted on entry but research continued per explicit human invocation.

hypothesis: Bid-ask spread conditioned skip: at order submission, compute current spread from top-of-book quote. Track a rolling window of 60 recent spread values. Skip open (non-reduce-only) orders when spread > 2.0 × median(recent_spreads). Reduce-only orders always execute. Wide spreads signal high uncertainty regimes where the oracle's noisy 30s forecast is less reliable. This is distinct from prior imbalance-skip (which used bid/ask depth ratio) — spread width captures a different dimension of market-maker uncertainty.
notes: FAIL — aggregated over all 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): spread-filter $1622.50/5510 trades vs simple $1586.75/5522 trades; delta_pnl=+2.25%, below the 3% CLOSE threshold. Win rate improved slightly (48.44% vs 48.32%). Slippage: both 0.0 (neutral). CRITICAL CONTEXT: sigma was changed from 0.5 to 5 in commit ab2360b between this iteration and all prior ones, reducing oracle win rate from ~84-85% to ~48% (near-random). All prior program_database scores are incomparable — they reflect a much higher-quality signal. The spread filter is directionally correct (positive delta) but fires too rarely (skip rate ~0.2%, -12 trades vs baseline) to overcome the noise in the low-sigma oracle. With sigma=5, the execution algo must identify losing trades in a near-coin-flip signal environment — a harder problem than at sigma=0.5. Human operator action needed: clarify whether sigma=5 is intentional. Suggested next: try lower spread threshold (1.2-1.5x) for higher skip rate, or composite filter combining spread + momentum.

hypothesis: Order-Flow Imbalance conditioned skip: compute a rolling EMA(N=20) of OFI = (bid_qty_delta - ask_qty_delta) per quote tick. Skip open orders when EMA(OFI) < -0.5 for BUY (adverse selling flow) or > +0.5 for SELL (adverse buying flow). Motivated by Kolm et al. (2023) finding that flow-based (stationary) features beat static book state for short-horizon price prediction. Orthogonal to spread-based approaches — OFI varies even when bid-ask spread is constant at 1 tick.
notes: FAIL — aggregated over 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): ofi-skip $1602.00 / 5462 trades vs simple $1586.75 / 5522 trades; delta_pnl = +0.96%, below both the 5.0% gate and the 3.0% CLOSE threshold. Per-date: 20260308 +0.53% (4 skipped), 20260309 +2.07% (31 skipped), 20260310 -0.61% (25 skipped). OFI filter fired on ~60 trades total (1.1% skip rate). Directionally positive on 20260309 but harmful on 20260310. Root cause: sigma=5 oracle with ~48% win rate cannot be selectively improved by low-frequency microstructure signals. The EMA-OFI threshold of 0.5 lots fires on persistent adverse flow only, which is rarer than individual tick events. Suggested next: try reduce-only order timing optimization or a fundamentally different architecture. Seven consecutive FAIL outcomes, all single-digit PnL improvements, consistently below the 5% gate with sigma=5. Human review of sigma=5 research setting is recommended.

hypothesis: Skip the OPEN leg of an oracle signal when the immediately preceding closed position suffered a per-trade realized P&L <= -3.0 USD (>= 12-tick adverse move). Uses quote-tick-based P&L estimation at open-order decision time to avoid on_order_filled sequencing issues. A _position_flat flag forces re-entry after any skip to prevent cascade. Reduce-only (close) orders always execute.
notes: PASS — aggregated over 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): pnl-regime-skip $1676.50/5401 trades vs simple $1586.75/5522 trades; delta_pnl=+5.66%, above the 5.0% gate. Slippage 0.0 (neutral). Per-date: 20260308 +1.25% ($142.25/337 vs $140.50/351), 20260309 +6.86% ($927.25/2793 vs $867.75/2863), 20260310 +4.93% ($607.00/2271 vs $578.50/2308). Sharpe (mean across dates): 82.00 + 135.55 + 105.96 = avg 107.84. CAVEAT: The -3.0 USD threshold was selected by in-sample analysis of the same 3 training dates; constitutes mild parameter fitting. OOS Lambda evaluation will be the true test. Implementation used quote-tick-based P&L estimation to avoid Nautilus event-ordering issues with on_order_filled; _position_flat flag prevents skip cascade.

hypothesis: Combined post-loss regime skip AND wide-spread skip: skip OPEN orders when EITHER (a) the immediately preceding closed position suffered a realized P&L <= -3.0 USD (12+ tick adverse move), OR (b) the current bid-ask spread exceeds 1.5x the rolling 60-tick median spread. The two signals are orthogonal: PnL signal captures temporal regime persistence; spread signal captures contemporaneous market-maker uncertainty. OR combination targets different adverse trade types. Builds on pnl-regime-skip (PASS +5.66%) by adding spread as a second skip trigger. One targeted change vs parent.
notes: PASS — aggregated over 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): pnl-spread-skip $1840.00/5296 trades vs simple $1586.75/5522 trades; delta_pnl=+15.96%, above the 5.0% gate. Per-date: 20260308 +5.16% ($147.75/333 vs $140.50/351), 20260309 +15.99% ($1006.50/2762 vs $867.75/2863), 20260310 +18.54% ($685.75/2201 vs $578.50/2308). Slippage 0.0 (neutral). Win rate: 49.45% vs 48.32% (+1.14 pp). Mean Sharpe: 117.65 vs 99.78. Max drawdown: -0.3349% vs -0.4298% (improved). REFINEMENT vs pnl-regime-skip: +9.75% PnL delta (target +2%), +9.81 Sharpe delta (target +0.10) — both exceeded. CAVEAT: Dual in-sample parameter fitting (PnL -3.0 and spread 1.5x both from same training window). OOS Lambda will be the true test.

hypothesis: AND-combination PnL-regime + spread skip: skip OPEN orders only when BOTH (a) the immediately preceding closed position suffered P&L <= -3.0 USD AND (b) current spread > 1.5x rolling 60-tick median spread. Higher precision than the OR variant (pnl-spread-skip PASS +15.96%); targets only the intersection where both adverse signals fire simultaneously. One targeted change vs parent: OR -> AND, same thresholds.
notes: CLOSE — aggregated over 3 train dates (20260308, 20260309, 20260310): pnl-spread-skip-and $1631.00/5506 trades vs simple $1586.75/5522 trades; delta_pnl=+2.79%, above close_margin_pct (2.0%) but below pass gate (5.0%). Per-date: 20260308 +4.09% ($146.25/350 vs $140.50/351), 20260309 +3.34% ($896.75/2852 vs $867.75/2863), 20260310 +1.64% ($588.00/2304 vs $578.50/2308). Slippage 0.0 (neutral). Total AND-skips: 16 across 3 dates (vs 226 OR-skips in parent pnl-spread-skip). RESULT WARNING: only 16 skip decisions across 3 dates — statistical confidence in the +2.79% is low. Hypothesis CONTRADICTED: the two signals almost never co-occur at the same tick (both are time-localized differently — PnL fires right after a loss, spread fires during wide-spread moments; these rarely coincide). The AND criterion achieves ~7% of the parent OR variant's P&L gain with ~7% of the skips — not higher precision, just lower recall. Refinement NOT successful: parent pnl-spread-skip at +15.96% remains the superior algorithm. Suggested next: time-of-day skip filter, or 2-skip-window variant of the OR combination.
